title: fix(desktop): webcam track recorder and library follow-ups (NIW2-581)
body:
Follow-up to the webcam-track stack (#437 → #441 … #446), Linear [NIW2-581](https://linear.app/niway/issue/NIW2-581). Base: `feature/niw2-576-webcam-share-protect` ([#446](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/446)).

## What this does

Picks up the recorder, writer and library nits the reviewers of [#441](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/441), [#442](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/442), [#443](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/443) and [#446](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/446) declined, plus the residual risk #446 left documented:

- **A lost webcam file is now reported.** If a take recorded a webcam file but the saved recording has none (its encoder failed, it did not finalize at stop, or main could not place it), the user sees a toast after the take: "We couldn't save your camera recording, so your face may be missing from this video. The screen recording was kept." The screen recording is saved as before.
- **Stop always releases the camera**, even when the screen file fails to finalize.
- **The start offset is exact more often**: a first-media time the live 3 s wait gave up on is read again after stop.
- **Stranded takes and salvage are safer**: a broken webcam part is not kept for salvage, and salvage never overwrites an existing `<name>.webcam.mp4`.
- **Old Windows asks instead of being refused**: a capability flag replaces the `[webcam:unsupported]` refusal; behaviour on Windows before 10 2004 is unchanged.
- Library: one predicate for "has a webcam track"; remove-local-copy no longer hashes the file for a refusal that does not need the hash.

## Why

The face must never silently disappear. #446 made the bubble leave the capture while a webcam file records; if that file then failed at stop, nothing told the user the face was in no file. The rest are the review nits that keep the recorder and the library honest (camera light, broken parts handed to salvage, a file overwritten without a confirm, two readers of the same fact that could drift).

## What to review

1. `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.ts:1015`: the not-saved notice. It fires when the engine had a webcam handle and the saved recording carries no `webcam`. Check the condition cannot fire for a take with the camera off, and does not double up with `webcamUnavailable`.
2. `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:828`: `stop()` now wraps both finalizes in `try/finally`; a screen finalize failure cancels the webcam output and still stops every track and closes the audio context.
3. `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:907` and `first-media-timestamp.ts:54`: `startTimesAfterStop()` / `rereadFirstMediaTimestamp`. mediabunny never resets `_firstMediaStreamTimestamp` (set once in `media-source.js`, initialised in `output.js`), so reading it after stop is safe.
4. `apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-store.ts:473`: the capability is asked per take, before the webcam session. The webcam create still leaves after the screen create (main's `BubbleProtection` relies on that order). An unanswered capability call falls back to asking main, which still refuses on old Windows (`recording-hub.ts:398`).
5. `apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/recording-writer.ts:322` (`strand`) and `:394` (salvage picks `<name>.webcam-<n>.mp4` when `<name>.webcam.mp4` exists).
6. `apps/kaipu-record/src/main/library/webcam-track-state.ts`: the shared predicate. Behaviour is unchanged: the file alone makes a track "present" (protected from remove-local-copy), and `describe()` only returns a sanitized meta.

**Safe to skim:** the rename `fullDisplayBorderAllowed` → `canExcludeWindowFromCapture` (mechanical), `electron-api.ts`/`preload`/`ipc.ts` plumbing, the i18n strings, the docs and the tests.

## Decisions

| id | outcome |
| --- | --- |
| S3 | **done**: `WebcamHandle.startTimesAfterStop()` re-reads both outputs' first-media time where the live wait returned "estimated"; the store builds the offset from it. |
| S4 | **done**: documented on `EngineHandle.pause` and in the spec (section 2), which wrongly said the offset stays constant. Each source drops paused time in steps of its own frames, so a pause can shift the webcam by up to about one webcam frame (33 ms) and several pauses add up: ±1 frame per pause at worst. A pause before the webcam's first frame is not dropped from the webcam: the webcam plays late by the paused time. That window is about one frame after the take begins, so it is documented, not corrected. |
| S5 | **done**: `strand()` discards a webcam session whose write failed or that finalize carried no usable meta for (the rule `placeWebcam` already applied). |
| S6 | **done**: salvage keeps an existing `<name>.webcam.mp4`; the webcam takes the first free `<name>.webcam-<n>.mp4`. The save dialog only confirmed replacing the screen file. |
| S8 | **done**: devices are released in a `finally`; a failed screen finalize also cancels the webcam output (the take fails, the webcam file has nothing to belong to). |
| S9 | **done**: `endWebcam` does not `close()` a source whose encoder failed; it still stops the camera track. |
| V1 | **done**: `webcamTrackState(fileExists, sidecarWebcam)` is the one rule; `probeWebcam` uses its `state`, `describe()` its `meta`. The disagreement #442 noted stays on purpose: a file without a valid field is "present" (protected) with `meta: null` (a recovered take gets no field). |
| V2 | **done**: `removeLocalCopy` checks the edit session, then the webcam, and hashes only when neither refuses. Same reasons, same order. |
| W3 | **declined**: keeping a saved layer while the file is missing is more than "a signal from describe". The signal itself is small (the predicate already has `"missing"`), but a kept `scene.webcam` with no file reaches the lane (`video-editor-page.tsx:1289` renders on `scene.webcam` alone), the export plan (`plan.webcam` non-null, so `faceDropped` and its notice fire), the GIF path and the edit fingerprint. Doing it right means splitting the persisted scene from the effective one in the editor controller and the autosave. Too large and too risky for a nit stack with no owner QA. Recorded as still open in `backlog/webcam-track.md`. |
| F4 | **done**: `recordingWebcamTrackSupported()` (new IPC) tells the renderer whether this OS can exclude the bubble. The recorder opens no webcam session where it cannot. `WEBCAM_TRACK_UNSUPPORTED_MARKER` is removed; main keeps a plain refusal as a backstop. `fullDisplayBorderAllowed` is renamed `canExcludeWindowFromCapture`. Old Windows: no webcam file, bubble in the screen, no notice, as before. |
| R1 | **done**: `kind` and `purpose` are required on `recordingCreate`; the recorder passes `"screen"`/`"webcam"` and `"take"`. Main still reads anything but `"export"` as a take (IPC input stays untrusted). |
| #446 residual risk 2 | **done** (reported, not prevented): the post-take toast above. Residual risk 1 (a running ScreenCaptureKit stream may not pick up an unprotected bubble mid-take) is unchanged and still waits on the spike ([#440](https://github.com/niway-dev/kaipu-record/pull/440)). |

New user-facing string: `record.webcamNotSaved` (en, es).

## Checks

- `cd apps/kaipu-record && node_modules/.bin/vitest run`: exit 0, 326 files, 3336 tests passed (baseline on the base branch: 325 files, 3317 tests).
- `cd apps/kaipu-record && bun run check-types`: exit 0.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint` (repo root): 0 errors, 18 warnings, all already there, none in touched files.
- Pre-push `verify:local` (lint, oxfmt, build, check-types): passed on push.
- Not run: Electron, the app, the Playwright E2E suite (agents do not run them on the owner's machine). Nothing here is verified on a real take.

## How to test it yourself

**Setup:** `git checkout feature/niw2-581-webcam-recorder-followups && bun install && bun run dev`.

1. **Normal take, camera on.** Record 10 s with the camera on, stop. Expect: no toast, the recording opens in the editor with its webcam layer, and the camera light goes off at stop.
2. **Take with the camera off.** Record 5 s, stop. Expect: no toast.
3. **Webcam lost mid-take.** Start a take with the camera on, unplug an external camera (or turn the camera off from the bar) after 3 s, record 3 s more, stop. Expect: the recording saves; no "not saved" toast (the file ends where you unplugged it and is still saved).
4. **The not-saved toast.** There is no reliable way to make the webcam file fail by hand (it needs an encoder or muxer failure at stop). The unit tests cover it (`recorder-store.test.ts`, "a webcam file that did not make it into the recording"). If you ever see it after a real take, check that the screen recording opened normally.
5. **Salvage does not overwrite.** Point the vault at a folder you then make unwritable (or unplug the drive) before stopping a camera-on take; when the save dialog appears, choose a name next to an existing `<name>.webcam.mp4`. Expect: `<name>.mp4` saved, the old `<name>.webcam.mp4` untouched, the new webcam saved as `<name>.webcam-2.mp4`.
6. **Remove local copy** (signed in, item uploaded): on a recording with a webcam file, "Remove local download" is still refused with the webcam reason, and it answers at once even for a long recording.
7. **Old Windows** (only if you have a Windows build before 10 2004): a camera-on take records no webcam file, the bubble is in the screen recording, and no toast appears.
